text:
maria: Heads up — saw an oddity this morning where an EU telemetry backfill got routed into the low-priority GPU pool. Recompute stalled for ~2 hours. Anyone else see routing noise?

jonathan: saw alerts for increased queue depth, thought it was normal burst. didn't check pool mapping. Can you paste the job id?

maria: job=rbk-recompute-2026-03-21-33, logs attached in cloud-storage. Key symptom: router chose `cheap-spot` policy instead of `eu-priority`.

kevin: that's the same policy that used to be fallback when quota tokens expired. Did the token lease system fail?

lia: quick check — token ledger shows leases OK. But there was a routing policy reload at ~03:17 UTC from rollout v3.2.7. Could be a config mismatch between controller and router-mesh.

maria: putting the relevant snippet: ```json
{"routing_policies": [{"id":"eu-priority","pools":["dedicated-eu"],"priority":100},{"id":"cheap-spot","pools":["spot-global"],"priority":10}]}
```

peggy: that JSON looks right. If controller had stale view, router might apply the lower priority. We should check controller -> router diff. I can run a quick `diff` on the manifest states.

jonathan: also saw the console showed the job as "green" (running) but the per-route dashboard showed 0 tokens consumed for dedicated-eu. UI and infra disagree. UX bug?

lia: could be metric aggregation lag. The console polls the control plane; if control plane thinks it's routed to spot pool, console will show that. Let's triage: 1) confirm controller config at 03:10-03:20 2) confirm router-mesh applied snapshot 3) check lease/token expiry 4) run controlled re-route for a small sample job.

maria: I'll take 1 and 2. kevin take 3? jonathan/peggy handle 4?

kevin: on it. Checking kms logs for lease renewals... nothing abnormal. Token renews look fine.

peggy: can we test a controlled re-route without touching production? Maybe spawn a small replay with a tag to force eu-priority and watch routing.

jonathan: yes — propose a canary: run 50-job micro-recompute in eu with tag `canary-routing-2026-03-21`. If router misroutes, we'll see mismatch in pool assignment and token drain.

maria: agree. here's the API call I'll use to pin policy for the job: ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.internal/redwood/v1/jobs/recompute \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' \n  -d '{"dataset":"telemetry","range":"2026-03-20","policy":"eu-priority","tags":["canary-routing-2026-03-21"]}'
```

jonathan: note: admin API will respect controller snapshots. If controller is stale, we should push patch to router-mesh to force mesh refresh: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/router-mesh -n inference`

lia: I checked the controller snapshots — there was a migration script that temporarily changed policy IDs (s/priority->prio). Router-mesh expects `priority`; controller shipped with `prio` for a minute then fixed. If router validated strictly, it would have fallen back. This explains the window.

maria: ack — that matches the ~03:17 rollout. So root cause = schema drift during a migration window.

kevin: mitigation: add a tolerant parser to router that treats `prio`==`priority` for one release, and add a preflight check in rollout pipeline to detect key renames.

peggy: console UX note: when controller and router disagree we should surface a cross-check warning on the job details page: "control-plane vs data-plane mismatch" and link to the last applied snapshots. I'll open a small PR for a console banner.

sasha: ops-bot: can you tag the impacted jobs and add a follow-up incident?

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-153. Tagged 12 impacted backfills. Notifying infra-oncall. :white_check_mark:

jonathan: next steps: 1) run the 50-job canary now 2) if canary routes correctly, resume pending EU backfills 3) add rollout preflight and parser tolerance 4) console banner PR 5) postmortem in postmortems channel.

maria: starting canary in ~5m, will paste job ids. If we see any misroutes, we'll pause and roll back controller to pre-migration snapshot.

kevin: I'll prepare a quick revert manifest just in case.

peggy: PR for console banner opened: #4824. It adds a small red badge and a link to applied snapshots.

lia: filing a CI gate to validate config key names during migrations — preventing future s/priority->prio/ accidents.

maria: thanks all. Will update this thread with canary results. :mag_right:

(10 minutes later)

maria: canary finished — 50 jobs all routed to dedicated-eu. No stalls. Looks like routers got fixed after the migration completed.

jonathan: great. I'll resume the queued EU backfills gradually (rate 0.5x) and watch queue depth.

peggy: adding a console note on the resumed run for auditors.

maria: closing loop: root cause = transient schema rename during migration. Mitigations: tolerant parser, rollout preflight, console mismatch banner, and slower resume. I'll draft the postmortem and link to INC-2026-153.

sasha: thanks — nice quick triage. :tada:
